column2: Authoring source for every Claude Code adapter wrapper in kit/.
`scripts/generate-adapters.py` regenerates kit/.claude and kit/.agent-kit/catalog.txt from this
file. CI fails if the payload has drifted from it.
Tab-separated. Empty columns are written as a single "-".
kind      one of: workflow | skill | role
name      file/slug name; workflows also need kit/.agent-kit/workflows/<name>.md
title     used as "Execute the canonical <title> with ..."
desc      wrapper frontmatter description — this is how Claude Code decides to surface it
also      extra canonical file the wrapper must read (workflows), or "refs" for skills
note      extra sentence appended to the wrapper body

column4: Single entry point — route to the right kit workflow (ship, fix, debug, infra, riff) or bootstrap.
Ship one feature end-to-end; interaction ends at design approval, then work autonomously to PR.
Configure local or cloud infrastructure through the canonical interactive workflow.
Standalone product brainstorm — generate and stress-test ideas, roadmap the survivors. Builds nothing.
Lightweight path for a small, local, low-risk change — understand, change, test, review, PR.
Systematic debugging — reproduce, isolate, find root cause, then fix with a regression test or diagnose.
Run an independent, read-only adversarial review of the current changes or branch diff.
Add or improve tests for a named target, then run the project's test and lint suite.
Reconcile the living documentation standalone — update only where docs genuinely diverged.
Use before implementing any feature: clarify behavior, compare approaches, get design approval, write the spec.
Use when the project has no manifest or is not bootstrapped: interview the owner and set the project up.
Use after a design is approved, to turn the spec into an implementation plan with file boundaries and verification.
Use to think about what to build — a broad product riff, or scoping one already-chosen feature before design.
Use after a feature PR is open, to check whether the living docs still match what the code does.
Use to get the project running locally: containerize the backend and wire any dev mobile build.
Use to deploy the project: pick a host, generate deploy config and CI, guide owner-only provisioning.
Independent adversarial implementation diff reviewer. Read-only.
Independent tester that adds missing tests and hunts edge cases.
